title: crumb: how does a running state-mode session autosave storage state to the vault?
scope: Timer-driven saves in supervise(): snapshot cookies, localStorage and IndexedDB, merge with the vault entry, rewrite it.
omissions: Launch, run handle files, signal-driven saves (crumb sync/close)
Profile mode (same timer, persistent profile), agent CDP, login/check

groups.label: Local machine
groups.description: Local host; all three as one OS user

nodes.label: Supervisor
nodes.description: supervise(): owns Chrome, merges in memory

nodes.label: Chrome
nodes.description: Owned child, temp profile; close skips save

notes.title: Timer, skip, retry
notes.text: Default 30s; --autosave 0 = off. Ticks join an in-flight save; unchanged state skips. Errors go only to the ~/.crumb/run log; before advances only on success, so the next tick retries.

notes.title: Merge in memory, no lock
notes.text: Between steps 3 and 4, only before → after changes are applied to the latest entry, plus sync provenance and browser hints. No lock: another process's write in that window is lost.

notes.title: Key cached at startup
notes.text: Key: CRUMB_KEY, else config.json's keyStore (Keychain, Secret Service or ~/.crumb/key). Cached at startup, so saves make no key-store calls. Body is AES-256-GCM; header is plaintext.
